terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; the thing in the accusative, the person in the dative
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.35: honor nōn sōlum datus sed etiam crēditus ac commissus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Mil. 70: cum senātus eī commīserit, ut vidēret, nē quid rēs pūblica dētrīmentī caperet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its other common senses are to join battle (proelium committere, Caes. BG 2.21) and to commit a wrong (quī nihil commīserint, Cic. Mil. 61) (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cum senātus eī commīserit, ut vidēret, nē quid rēs pūblica dētrīmentī caperet
phrases.english: since the senate has entrusted him with seeing that the state takes no harm
